questions.stem: What is the role of `next()` in Express middleware?
choices: Passes control to the next middleware in the stack
questions.explanation: next() hands off to the next middleware. Forgetting to call it (and not ending the response) leaves the request hanging.

questions.stem: An Express error-handling middleware is identified by:
choices: Having four parameters: (err, req, res, next)
questions.explanation: Express inspects function arity. Four args marks it as error middleware, called when next(err) is invoked.

questions.stem: Which Express middleware parses JSON request bodies?
questions.explanation: express.json() reads the body, parses it as JSON, and attaches it to req.body. Mount it before routes that need it.

questions.stem: Where does Node best fit?
choices: IO-heavy concurrent workloads (web servers, proxies, real-time)
questions.explanation: Node's non-blocking IO and event loop excel at many concurrent IO operations. Heavy CPU blocks the loop and hurts throughput.

questions.stem: Given route /users/:id?role=admin, where does Express place the 'admin' value?
questions.explanation: Path params (?:id) live on req.params. Query string values live on req.query. Body fields on req.body.

choices: E C D A B (A/B order may swap)
questions.explanation: Sync first (E). Then process.nextTick (C), then microtasks (D). Then timers (A) and immediate (B), whose relative order depends on context.

questions.stem: Which HTTP status code is appropriate when a POST successfully creates a resource?
questions.explanation: 201 with a Location header pointing to the new resource is the REST convention.

questions.stem: Which middleware order is correct?
choices: Body parser, then routes, then error middleware
questions.explanation: Express runs middleware in declaration order. Parsers must run before handlers that read the body; error middleware is last so it catches downstream errors.

questions.stem: What does `app.use(express.static('public'))` do?
choices: Serves files in ./public as static assets at the matching URL paths
questions.explanation: express.static turns a directory into a file server. /style.css resolves to ./public/style.css.

questions.stem: What is `res.sendStatus(404)` equivalent to?
questions.explanation: sendStatus sets the status code and sends the default reason phrase as the body.

questions.stem: Why is process.nextTick described as 'starve the loop' risky?
choices: Its callbacks run before IO, so an infinite chain prevents IO events from being processed
questions.explanation: nextTick queue is drained between phases, ahead of IO. Recursively queuing nextTicks can prevent timers/IO from ever running.

questions.stem: Why use streams instead of reading a 1GB file into memory?
choices: Lower memory footprint and immediate downstream progress
Streams are faster only for small files
questions.explanation: Streams process chunks incrementally so peak memory stays small. They also begin sending bytes to the client immediately.

questions.stem: An Express handler throws inside an async function but does not catch. In Express 4 default behaviour:
choices: The request hangs because the error never reaches error middleware
questions.explanation: Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async handlers. You must wrap with asyncH or call next(err). Express 5 changes this.

questions.stem: Which is the right module spec to import the built-in HTTP module?
questions.explanation: Use the node: prefix to explicitly import core modules; safer against future shadowing by npm packages.

questions.stem: What does `app.use((req, res, next) => { next(); })` accomplish if it does nothing else?
choices: Acts as a no-op pass-through in the chain
questions.explanation: Calling next() with no error simply continues to the next middleware. Useful as a debug logger or to set req values.

questions.stem: Why mount express.json() before a POST route that reads req.body?
choices: Middleware runs in declaration order — the body must be parsed before the handler accesses it
questions.explanation: Express middleware is order-sensitive. If the parser hasn't run, req.body is undefined when the handler executes.

questions.stem: Which is true about non-blocking IO in Node?
choices: Each request runs on a new OS thread
IO operations are queued to libuv; their callbacks fire on completion via the event loop
questions.explanation: libuv uses a thread pool for filesystem IO and the OS event mechanisms for network IO, calling back into JS when ready.

questions.stem: What does `res.json(obj)` do?
choices: Sets Content-Type to application/json, JSON.stringifies obj, and sends it
questions.explanation: Convenience shorthand: it serialises the object and sets the JSON content type.

questions.stem: Which file should NOT be committed to source control?
questions.explanation: .env carries secrets. Add it to .gitignore and commit a .env.example with the names of required variables only.

questions.stem: Which is the correct way to define a route param?
questions.explanation: Express uses :name syntax. The captured value is on req.params.name.

questions.stem: What is the default port pattern?
choices: Read from process.env.PORT with a development fallback
questions.explanation: Cloud platforms inject PORT. Hard-coding breaks deployment; reading from env with a fallback handles both.

questions.stem: Why is a long synchronous loop in a Node handler harmful?
choices: It blocks the single-threaded event loop, freezing every concurrent request
It can only run during startup
questions.explanation: Node serves all requests on one main thread. A long CPU loop monopolises it until completion.

questions.stem:
What does `pipe` do here?

req.pipe(res);
choices: Echoes the request body back to the client with backpressure handling
questions.explanation: pipe forwards chunks from a readable to a writable stream, pausing the source when the destination is full.

questions.stem: Which is true about Router?
choices: An express.Router() lets you group related routes/middleware and mount them at a path prefix
Router is only for static files
questions.explanation: Routers modularise endpoints. app.use('/api/v1', router) mounts the router under that prefix.

choices: Routes after error middleware are skipped only when next(err) is called earlier
Error middleware at the top intercepts all requests
The error middleware needs to be a route
questions.explanation: Error middleware only runs when an upstream next(err) is invoked. Normal requests skip it and flow to the route. Best practice is still to mount it last.
